problem: Existing embodied AI simulators target indoor households, road driving, or oversimplified crowd navigation, so none supports urban micromobility (sidewalks, plazas) with large scale, varied terrain, diverse real-world obstacles and dense pedestrians.
motivation: Delivery bots, wheelchairs, robot dogs and humanoids now share public urban spaces with pedestrians, so the generalizability and safety of their AI policies must be trained and tested in simulation first. Urban micromobility poses unique challenges (long-horizon large scenes, multifarious terrains, diverse obstacles, dense pedestrians) that indoor or driving simulators do not cover.
key_idea: A compositional procedural simulator (MetaUrban) builds infinite interactive urban scenes from hierarchical layouts, VLM-retrieved real-distribution obstacles, and populated pedestrians/VRUs/machines, together with the MetaUrban-12K dataset and PointNav/SocialNav benchmarks.
insight: Training on many compositional scenes improves generalization: PPO SR rises from 12% to 46% as training scenes grow from 5 to 1,000, and models trained on MetaUrban-12K keep about 49% SR on unseen scenes. Pretraining on MetaUrban-train then fine-tuning clearly beats training from scratch on the small unseen-distribution set (Setting-4 vs Setting-3). Machine mechanics matter: the conservative wheelchair is safest but least mobile, while lowering COCO's max speed to 10 km/h improves both mobility and safety. Tasks remain unsolved, and SocialNav is much harder than PointNav.
method: Hierarchical Layout Generation: samples 5 street block types (straight, intersection, roundabout, circle, T-junction), 7 sidewalk templates with four functional zones (from the Global Street Design Guide), crosswalks, and places standard infrastructure, non-standard infrastructure and clutter by zone and density.
Terrain generation: connects sampled terrain primitives (slopes, steps, stairs, ramps, rough) using Wave Function Collapse for smooth transitions, with friction textures.

Scalable Obstacle Retrieval: builds a 1,215-item real-world description pool from Cityscapes/Mapillary (90), 25k Google Street images analyzed with GPT-4o and Grounded-SAM (1,075), and urban design handbooks (50); retrieves assets from Objaverse/XL by BLIP image-text matching with informative-view selection, then manual curation, giving 10,000 obstacles.

Cohabitant Populating: 1,100 SMPL-X rigged humans (SynBody assets), 2,311 BEDLAM motions plus daily motions, VRUs (bikers, skateboarders, scooter riders), 6 mobile machines and 37 vehicles; trajectories from ORCA plus Push-and-Rotate for collision and deadlock avoidance.
User interfaces: mouse, keyboard, joystick and racing wheel for collecting human demonstrations and for scene customization.

MetaUrban-12K and benchmarks: 12,800 train scenes, 1,000 test, 100 unseen and 1,000 finetune scenes; PointNav and SocialNav with 7 baselines (PPO, PPO-Lag, PPO-ET, IQL, TD3+BC, BC, GAIL) using LiDAR observations and continuous acceleration/steering.

setting.backbone: Baseline RL/IL policies (PPO, PPO-Lag, PPO-ET, IQL, TD3+BC, BC, GAIL) trained from scratch on LiDAR state vectors
setting.training_data: MetaUrban-train (12,800 procedurally generated scenes); offline RL/IL use 30,000 steps of demonstrations (20% human, 80% PPO expert, ~60% SR)
setting.observation: LiDAR vector (50 m range) + ego state vector + navigation info toward the destination (RGB, depth, semantic also available but unused)
setting.privileged: none stated (navigation information toward the destination is given, no pre-built map)

numbers_note: Benchmarks are the paper's own MetaUrban-12K tasks, not canonical ones; 'test' means MetaUrban-test, and entries marked unseen use MetaUrban-unseen. Table 1 includes seven baselines; only a few are listed here. Cross-machine and ablation results are in Table 2 and Figure 3.
results: Baselines are far from solving the tasks: the best PointNav SR is 66% (PPO) and the best SocialNav SR is 36% (IQL) on test. Generalization to unseen scenes is decent (average 41% PointNav, 26% SocialNav SR). Safe RL cuts cost at some cost in success, and SR scales from 12% to 46% with more training scenes.
limitations: No real-world experiments in the paper; sim-to-real is only discussed, and rendering and physics are lightweight (PyBullet/Panda3D).

Environmental agents follow deterministic rule-based ORCA/P&R trajectories, not interactive or social behaviors, and object locations and layouts are not drawn from real-world distributions (only categories are).
Simulation efficiency degrades as scale, object count and agent count grow; only navigation with LiDAR baselines is evaluated, with no vision or foundation-model baselines.
